candidate.answerReason: Exactly three of the eight equally likely sequences contain consecutive heads: HHH, HHT, and THH. The probability is 3/8, matching choice C.

methods.label: List the possible sequences
methods.explanation:
Write \(H\) for heads and \(T\) for tails. The three fair tosses give eight equally likely ordered sequences:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&HHH,\ HHT,\ HTH,\ HTT,\\
&THH,\ THT,\ TTH,\ TTT.
\end{aligned}
\]
This list includes both possibilities at each position, with no sequence repeated.

A consecutive pair of heads must occupy either the first two tosses or the last two tosses. Exactly \(HHH\), \(HHT\), and \(THH\) qualify. We count \(HHH\) once, even though it contains two adjacent pairs of heads. Thus the probability is
\[
\frac{3}{8},
\]
choice C.
methods.levelReason: Listing eight outcomes and taking the favorable fraction is elementary counting and probability suitable for AMC 8.
